name: Pokereth-Hashshabaim
title: Descendant of Solomon's Servants
summary: Pokereth-Hashshabaim is mentioned as one of the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem. His descendants were among those who came back with Zerubbabel to rebuild the temple and restore the Jewish community in Judah. He represents the faithful remnant that preserved their family identity through the exile.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among the Descendants of Solomon's Servants
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Pokereth-Hashshabaim are mentioned in the list of those who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Nehemiah's List
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Pokereth-Hashshabaim are mentioned again in Nehemiah's parallel list of those who returned from the exile, confirming their place in the restored community.

keyEvents.title: Part of the Great Return Under Zerubbabel
keyEvents.description: Pokereth-Hashshabaim's family was among the many who returned to Judah under Zerubbabel's leadership as part of the first major return from Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Counting of the descendants of Solomon's servants
keyEvents.description: The total number of temple slaves and descendants of Solomon's servants who returned was counted as 392 people, and the family of Pokeret-Hassebaim was among them.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding the community in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: After returning home, the descendants of Solomon's servants, including the family of Pokeret-Hassebaim, contributed to the rebuilding of the Jewish community and temple service in Jerusalem.
